title: Fine-Tuning a Transducer for Impaired Speech: Where the Gains Appear and What They Mean for Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.07587v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speech recognition still works poorly for many people whose speech is affected by conditions such as ALS, Parkinson's disease, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome or stroke. We took part in the Speech Accessibility Project Challenge 2 (SAPC2) with a public speech recognizer that we fine-tuned on the challenge data. Our best entry scored 7.81% character error rate on Test1, the first of two hidden test sets (official baseline 15.26%). Our live entries ran on CPUs with a combined median latency of about 0.9 seconds at 7.96-8.07% error. On new speakers, fine-tuning reduced errors most for the speakers that an off-the-shelf recognizer finds hardest to understand. Sentences already seen in training had far lower error rates than new ones (2.58% vs 6.42%), a larger difference than being a familiar speaker made. We close with lessons for evaluating such systems.

translated_title: 针对障碍语音微调转换器模型：收益出现在何处及其对评估的意义
translated_abstract: 语音识别对许多因肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）、帕金森病、脑瘫、唐氏综合征或中风等疾病而影响发音的人群仍然效果不佳。我们使用一个在挑战赛数据上微调过的公开语音识别器参加了语音无障碍项目挑战赛2（SAPC2）。我们最好的参赛模型在两个隐藏测试集中的第一个Test1上取得了7.81%的字符错误率（官方基线为15.26%）。我们的实时参赛模型在CPU上运行，组合中位延迟约为0.9秒，错误率为7.96%-8.07%。对于新说话人，微调对现成识别器最难理解的说话人降低错误的效果最为显著。训练中已见过的句子比新句子的错误率低得多（2.58%对6.42%），这一差异大于说话人熟悉程度所带来的差异。我们最后以评估此类系统的经验教训作结。
tldr: 该论文在SAPC2挑战赛数据上微调公开语音识别器，将障碍语音识别的字符错误率从15.26%基线降至7.81%，并揭示微调收益最大来自现成模型最难理解的说话人，而训练中见过的句子的错误率显著低于新句子，且这一差距大于说话人熟悉度带来的影响。
en_tdlr: The paper fine-tunes a public speech recognizer on SAPC2 challenge data, cutting character error rate for impaired speech from a 15.26% baseline to 7.81%, and shows gains are largest for speakers hardest for off-the-shelf models, while sentences seen in training yield far lower error than novel ones—a larger gap than speaker familiarity itself.
